title: Metering for late prefetches and priority-queue interleaving
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: We are seeing incorrect token/quota attribution in production when speculative prefetches (late warmups) or high-priority short requests interleave with ongoing aggregated microbatches. Two common scenarios cause customer-visible issues: 1) a speculative KV prefetch is charged as a full reservation then later merged into an existing microbatch causing double-counting or lost attribution; 2) priority queue preemption inserts short, latency-sensitive requests into the middle of a large coalesced batch which changes how rate-limit windows and quotas should be decremented. Both lead to inaccurate billing, surprising quota consumption spikes, and inconsistent rate-limit behavior for tenants.
impact_summary: Customer-facing billing spikes (medium-high), quota enforcement surprises for bursty tenants (medium), incorrect cost breakdowns in Console (low-medium). Affects hosted API and Dedicated when prefetching and priority queues are enabled.
acceptance_criteria: New metering path assigns a stable 'provenance token' to speculative prefetches and microbatches, allowing post-hoc reconciliation without double charges.

Rate-limiter semantics updated: quota windows are decremented atomically at microbatch commit time but allow 'reservation holds' that are visible in dashboards and do not permanently consume quota until commit succeeds.

Unit and integration tests cover: prefetch-then-merge, prefetch-evict-then-commit, priority-insert-into-ongoing-batch, and multi-tenant interleaving. No regressions observed in existing metering tests.
Console shows separate metrics: reservation_holds, committed_tokens, reconciled_adjustments for at least 30d retention behind a feature flag.
Benchmark: end-to-end accounting mismatch <= 0.1% on synthetic workload with 40% speculative prefetch rate and 25% priority interleaving compared to ground-truth simulator.
proposal_summary: Introduce a two-stage accounting flow: (A) Reserve: when a speculative prefetch or request enters the system we allocate a lightweight 'reservation' record with a provenance id and the maximum potential token claim; this increments a reservation_gauge (not quota) and creates an audit trace. (B) Commit/Reconcile: when tokens are actually emitted (microbatch commit), the reservation is either consumed (matched by provenance id) or released and a final committed token count is attributed to the originating tenant(s) and microbatch owners. For interleaved priority inserts we ensure the commit step is single-threaded per microbatch to preserve atomic token accounting while allowing latency-priority fast-paths to splice into the pipeline without immediate quota mutation.
design_decisions: Use a provenance UUID per request/prefetch and attach it to microbatch metadata (immutable string). Provenance is used in metering logs and reconciliation jobs.
Reservations do NOT decrement tenant quota; they mark a hold metric and are visible in Console. Only commit decrements quota and billing counters.

When multiple reservations merge into one microbatch, commit logic performs deterministic attribution: primary owner(s) are charged proportional to final token emission by request weight heuristics (input tokens + declared max tokens).

Rate limiter update: support a 'soft reservation' state in token bucket that prevents over-commit but does not permanently remove capacity until commit succeeds; reservation expirations auto-release after configurable TTL (default 10s).

To avoid storage blowup, reservation records are stored in a compact append-only log for 72h and then summarized; reconciliation uses short-lived in-memory indexes and falls back to logs for audit queries.
implementation_plan: Create lightweight Reservation service: REST + in-memory cache + durable append-only log (team: serving-runtime).
Runtime: attach provenance id at request ingest and propagate through batching layer; add commit hook in microbatch commit path to call Reservation service reconciliation endpoint.
Quota/rate-limiter: implement soft-reservation state in token-bucket implementation; make reservation TTL and behavior configurable via feature flag.

Billing: update metering pipeline to report reservation_gauge, committed_tokens, and reconciliation_adjustments to the billing ledger and console. Add a short-term backfill job to reconcile historical mismatches for the previous 7 days.

Testing: develop deterministic simulator harness (unit/integration) that can re-run recorded traces with and without reservations to validate parity. Add chaos tests (evict prefetch mid-flight, microbatch commit failure, reservation log GC).
Docs & Console: Confluence doc, Console UI addition showing reservation holds per-tenant, and customer-facing KB explaining reservation semantics and expected behavior.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Reservation storage increases write volume. Mitigation: compact records and retain only 72h; sample long tails for audit instead of full retention.

Risk: Added latency for commit path due to reconciliation calls. Mitigation: reconciliation is async best-effort for billing pipes; commit must only ensure atomic local attribution then schedule reconciliation job; critical SLOs preserved by fast-path local accounting + background ledger ingestion.
Risk: Customer confusion over 'holds' vs billed tokens. Mitigation: Console UI and docs call this out and we expose a preview endpoint for customers to see reservation_holds in real time.

Risk: Race between reservation TTL expiry and late commit. Mitigation: TTL conservative default (10s) and TTL extensions allowed when microbatch indicates long-running tokens; reconciliation will backfill expired reservations and correct billing via adjustment entries.
testing_plan: Unit tests for Reservation service (create, commit, release, gc).
Integration test: end-to-end from request ingest -> speculative prefetch -> merge into microbatch -> commit and billing ledger entry.
Simulator: replay production traces with instrumented ground-truth accounting to assert final billed tokens match simulator output within 0.1%.
Load test: synthetic 5k RPS with 35% speculative prefetch and 20% priority interleaving to validate reservation store throughput and latency.
Chaos test: force microbatch commit failures and network partitions between runtime and reservation service, assert no permanent double-billing and reconciliation jobs correct state.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout to canary (internal + 5 customers) for 2 weeks observing reservation metrics and billing deltas.
Enable in staging for full traffic replay for 72h and validate reconciled adjustments <= 0.1% vs simulator.
Gradual ramp: 10% -> 50% -> 100% across regions with automated rollback triggers on reconciliation error rate > 0.5% or unexpected billing delta > 2%.
After 30d and stability validation, enable retention extension and retire the short-term backfill job.
